Guide · ready to go in 5 minutes

How Fraxx works.

Fraxx is your personal language app for travel and everyday life: words, sentences and idioms in lots of languages, with pronunciation, conjugation, grammar, menus and quizzes. Here you'll see in a few steps how to get started, and then everything Fraxx has to offer.

Open Fraxx →⤓ As PDF

Test version: Translating your own new words isn't available yet and will come in a later version. Everything else already works, even offline.

First steps

Five steps from opening the app for the first time to your first translation.

Step 1

Pick your language

Fraxx shows up in your browser's language right away. When you continue for the first time, Fraxx asks once which language you speak, and yours is already preselected. That's your Source language: menus, explanations and hints are written in it. You can change it any time later under ⚙. If your browser language isn't available yet, Fraxx starts in English.

Step 2

Let's go

The home page shows what Fraxx can do. At the top right you switch the language of the page. Let's go → opens the table of contents. Tap the logo to come back here any time.

Step 3

Open a topic

In Content you'll find all topics as boxes. Right at the front are the Essentials: around 110 sentences and words you'll need first on any trip, with their own boxes for greetings, politeness, emergencies and more. That's the best place to start. After that come idioms by topic (restaurant, hotel, pharmacy …), vocabulary by topic, and at the very end Business with sentences and words for meetings, emails, phone calls and negotiations. Open ▾ takes you straight in.

Step 4

Read, listen, remember

Each row shows one entry in all your languages. The speaker 🔊 reads it aloud, and gray notes explain special cases. The star ☆ adds the entry to your cheat sheet.

Step 5

Settings

Under ⚙ you choose your source language, proficiency level (A1 to C2), your languages and the design (Light or Dark). Your version is shown at the very top.

After installing

Set it up once, and Fraxx works even without internet.

  1. Download language packsUnder ⚙ → App, language packs & backup you download the languages you need. Each pack contains all translations, conjugations, grammar and menus for that language.
  2. Short home pageWhen installed as an app, Fraxx opens with a compact home page: a search field, tiles for all areas, your quiz progress and the areas you opened most recently. You can find the full introduction there under “What is Fraxx?” or by tapping the logo.
  3. Use it offlineEverything that's installed works without internet: on the plane, abroad without mobile data, or in a dead zone.
  4. Good voicesReading aloud uses your device's voices. On Mac and Windows, Chrome usually sounds the most natural. You can install more voices in your device's language settings.
  5. Back up your dataYour stars, progress and settings are stored on your device. Under ⚙ → App, language packs & backup you can download a backup and restore it whenever you need to.
  6. UpdatesWhen a new version is available, a dot appears on the ⚙. There you can see what's new and decide for yourself when to update.

Everything Fraxx can do

The areas at a glance – you'll find them all in the bar at the top.

☰ Content

Over 7,500 words, sentences and idioms sorted by topic: from restaurants to pharmacies, repair shops and government offices. Plus alphabetical lists for nouns, verbs, adjectives and more. The first tab, Essentials, collects the most important things to get started: greetings, politeness, getting understood, numbers, emergencies and the most necessary words, each topic in its own box. The last tab, Business, offers around 430 sentences and words like in a business language course: small talk, meetings, phone and video calls, emails, presenting, negotiating, job applications, customer service, business travel and numbers. The search field finds topics by name.

Translations and pronunciation

Each entry appears in all your languages side by side, nouns with their article, idioms translated by meaning. 🔊 reads aloud, a second tap stops it. With the pin you keep important entries at the top, and with A–Z you sort.

Verbs and conjugation

Verbs are conjugated in all languages: present, perfect, past and future. Conjugation ▸ opens the tables, and the tense buttons switch the tense.

§ Grammar

The most important rules of each language from A1 to C1, with examples you can listen to. Verbs & Endings shows ending tables and irregular verbs, Common mistakes the stumbling blocks for speakers of your language. Practice in quiz tests a chapter with fill-in-the-blank sentences.

Verbs & Endings

Endings at a glance: regular patterns, exceptions and the most important irregular verbs, each with an example.

🍽 Menu

Around 250 popular dishes and drinks per country with original names and explanations, plus coffee, beer and wine. Warnings show when a name means something different elsewhere. Order ▸ shows you how to order it.

★ Cheat sheet

Everything you've marked with the star, compact in one language: words, idioms and dishes. Print turns it into a handy sheet for your trip.

Quiz

Learn with four answers per question: Words & sentences or Grammar, in both directions, by level and topic. With 🔊 Listen things are only read aloud, so you can check whether you understand what's being said. Listening has its own progress. After three correct answers, an entry counts as learned, and your progress shows how far you've come.

On your phone

Same content, made for your thumb: rows become cards, and the bar sits at the top.

Quick tips

  • New to a language? Start with the Essentials and practice them in the quiz: choose “Essentials” under Area.
  • For work: in the quiz, choose “Business (all)” under Area and practice meetings, emails and negotiating.
  • Search finds words and sentences in your language. Under the search field, use Other language ▾ to pick one of your languages or all languages.
  • Proficiency level under ⚙ hides everything above your level, in the table, grammar and quiz.
  • Up to 5 languages fit side by side in the table: your source language and four more.
  • For languages with a different script (Arabic, Russian, Japanese …), the transcription appears in italics below.
  • The ? at the top right explains every feature in detail.
  • The health information comes without guarantee and is no substitute for professional advice. It helps you communicate with a doctor or pharmacist.

Have a great trip!
